title: Dumka
summary: Dumka is a city located in the state of Jharkhand, India, serving as the headquarters of the Dumka district and the Santhal Pargana region. Established as a significant administrative center, Dumka has a rich history and cultural heritage, with connections to various ethnic groups and religions.

sections.heading: Geographical and Administrative Significance
paragraphs: Dumka is situated at coordinates 24.27°N 87.25°E, with an average elevation of 137 metres (449 feet). As the headquarters of the Dumka district and the Santhal Pargana region, it plays a crucial role in local governance and administration.

sections.heading: Historical Context
paragraphs: Dumka has a complex history, with early inhabitants including the Paharias, identified by the Greek traveler Megasthenes. The city became strategically important during medieval times due to its geographical features and was governed by various powers including the Mughals and the British.

During the British Raj, Dumka was established as an independent district in 1865 and became the headquarters of the Santal Pargana district in 1872. Post-independence, it was promoted to a divisional headquarters in 1983 and became the sub-capital of Jharkhand on 15 November 2000.

sections.heading: Demographics and Culture
paragraphs: As of the 2011 census, Dumka has a population of 47,584, with a literacy rate of 89.92%, surpassing the state average. The demographic composition includes a majority of Hindus (79.06%), followed by Muslims (8.09%) and Christians (6.54%).
Dumka is culturally rich, hosting numerous Hindu temples and annual fairs such as the Hizla Mela, which attracts thousands of visitors.

sections.heading: Education and Economy
paragraphs: Dumka is home to various educational institutions, including Sido Kanhu Murmu University, established in 1992, and several schools that focus on improving academic performance through initiatives like Sampurna Shiksha Kavach.
The economy of Dumka is supported by agriculture, education, and emerging industries, including the establishment of a pilot training center in 2017.

sections.heading: Transport and Connectivity
paragraphs: Dumka has seen improvements in transportation, with the Jasidih-Dumka railway line established in 2011 and a growing network of road connections to nearby cities. The city is also served by several nearby airports, enhancing its accessibility.
